proposed_widenings.name: CastTimeEffectModeChoice.options[].duration
proposed_widenings.justification: Minor Creation lasts 'until the end of your next turn' while the spell's overall header duration is 1 hour. CastTimeEffectModeChoice option entries have no duration field, so there is no honest way to express that a specific effect mode expires earlier than the host spell's lifecycle. Including create_object or create_illusion in the Minor Creation option without a per-option duration would misrepresent the lifecycle in the tracer.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Minor Creation: 'It lasts until the end of your next turn.'

proposed_widenings.name: SpellMechanics.maxConcurrentInstances (or OngoingEffectMechanics equivalent)
proposed_widenings.justification: Prestidigitation can be cast repeatedly; the non-instantaneous effects from prior casts persist and stack. The spell imposes a cap of 3 simultaneously active non-instantaneous effects. No field on ActivationMechanics, OngoingEffectMechanics, or SpellMechanics tracks a per-spell-identity concurrent-instance limit.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

notes: The spell structurally fits activation → direct → CastTimeEffectModeChoice. Five of the six named effects (Sensory Effect, Fire Play, Clean or Soil, Minor Sensation, Magic Mark) are purely narrative with no mechanical atoms and correctly map to options with omitted effects. Minor Creation partially fits create_object (trinket) or create_illusion (illusory image), but (a) the trinket-vs-illusion branch would require a nested choice within the option which is explicitly unsupported, and (b) the 'end of next turn' duration cannot be expressed per-option. Both blocking gaps are missing fields on existing surface shapes, not missing v4 atoms.
